text: Room opened — goal: improve: Self-improvement: review prompts/engines/routing/own-code; auto-apply safe changes; pitch

name: Sprocket
text:
Run PR-Agent in parallel mode on *new contributors only* for one week, then switch to *all PRs* permanently.

New contributors need faster feedback to learn norms; limiting the scope first reduces risk while proving the value. The trade-off is slower detection of false positives in existing contributors, but that’s acceptable since the goal is improving contributor onboarding, not policing veterans. After one week, we’ll have data to justify expanding to all PRs without wasting compute on contributors who already know the rules.

name: Gauge
text: The real risk isn’t just slower false-positive detection—it’s training the team to treat *all* automated feedback as optional until it’s “proven” by a human. A better alternative is running PR-Agent in parallel mode on *all PRs* but *flagging* new contributors’ feedback as “priority review” for one week, forcing the team to engage with the output early. Settle it by measuring whether new contributors actually adopt the norms faster with prioritized feedback versus waiting for a phased rollout.

name: Overhaul
text: Run PR-Agent in parallel mode on *all PRs* but *flag* new contributors’ feedback as “priority review” for one week—this trains the team to treat automated feedback as critical for newcomers while avoiding the risk of normalizing it as optional. The cost is a slight increase in reviewer workload, but it ensures faster learning and safer scaling.

name: Ratchet
text:

Result: A one-week trial where new contributors’ PR-Agent feedback is marked as priority, proving its value while minimizing reviewer overload. Owner: Gauge.
